exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Planning a Trip to Dunhuang
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Have you decided where to go for the summer holiday, Tom?
Tom: Yes, I really want to visit Dunhuang in the northwest of China.
Mia: Dunhuang? What is so special about it?
Tom: It has hundreds of ancient caves full of beautiful wall paintings.
Mia: That sounds amazing. How will you get there?
Tom: I'll take the fast train and then a bus to the grottoes.
Mia: Will you climb the famous sand mountain too?
Tom: Of course. I want to watch the sunset over the desert.
Mia: Send me lots of photos when you arrive!
Tom: I promise I will.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 问 Tom 暑假去哪儿;Tom 想去中国西北的敦煌,因为那里有数百个满是壁画的古老洞窟;他打算先坐高铁再转公交去石窟,还要爬鸣沙山看沙漠日落;Mia 让他到了多拍照片,Tom 答应了。

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 About the Mogao Grottoes
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The Mogao Grottoes lie near the city of Dunhuang.
They were carved out of the rock over about a thousand years.
There are more than seven hundred caves in all.
Inside, the walls are covered with colourful paintings and statues.
Today the caves are protected, and visitors come from many countries to see them.
exercises.translation_cn: 莫高窟坐落在敦煌城附近;历经约一千年从岩石中开凿而成;共有七百多个洞窟;洞内墙壁布满彩色壁画和雕像;如今洞窟受到保护,各国游客纷纷前来参观。

questions.stem: Where do the Mogao Grottoes lie?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Looking at the Flying Apsaras
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Guide: Now look up at the wall in front of you. Can you see the flying figures?
Visitor: Yes! They look like dancers in the sky. Who are they?
Guide: They are the Apsaras, also called the Flying Immortals.
Visitor: Their scarves seem to move as if there were a wind.
Guide: That is the skill of the old painters. They painted these during the Tang Dynasty.
Visitor: The colours are still so bright after all these years.
Guide: That is why we keep the light very low, to protect them.
Visitor: Thank you. I will never forget these wonderful paintings.
exercises.translation_cn: 导游让游客抬头看墙上飞舞的人物;游客觉得他们像天空中的舞者,问是谁;导游说那是飞天,又称“飞行的神仙”,绘于唐代;色彩历经多年仍鲜亮,所以洞内灯光保持很暗以保护壁画;游客说永远不会忘记这些精美的画。

questions.stem: What does the guide ask the visitor to look at?
options: The flying figures on the wall.

questions.stem: What are the Apsaras also called?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 The Library Cave
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In 1900, a Taoist priest made an amazing discovery at Dunhuang.
While cleaning a cave, he found a small room that had been closed for hundreds of years.
Inside were thousands of old papers, scrolls and paintings.
Today this room is called the Library Cave.
The papers tell us much about life on the Silk Road, but no one knows why the room was sealed.
exercises.translation_cn: 1900年,一位道士在敦煌有了惊人的发现;他在清理洞窟时,发现一个封闭了数百年的小室;里面藏有成千上万的古老纸卷、卷轴和画作;这个小室如今被称为藏经洞;这些文书让我们了解丝路上的生活,但无人知道它为何被封。

questions.stem: Who made the discovery in 1900?

options: Thousands of old papers, scrolls and paintings.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 East Meets West
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Our history teacher said Dunhuang was a meeting point of East and West. Why?
Jack: Because the Silk Road passed right through it.
Lily: So traders from different lands all stopped there?
Jack: Yes, and they brought not only goods but also new ideas and art.
Lily: That must be why the cave paintings show so many cultures.
Jack: Exactly. Today the city holds a big cultural Expo every year.
Lily: I'd love to take part in it one day.
Jack: Me too. It's a great way to learn from other countries.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 问历史老师为何说敦煌是东西方交汇点;Jack 说因为丝绸之路正好穿城而过;各地商人都在此停留,带来货物,也带来新思想和艺术;这就是壁画展现多种文化的原因;如今城里每年举办大型文化博览会;两人都想有朝一日参加,因为这是向他国学习的好方式。

options: A meeting point of East and West.

questions.stem: Why was it a meeting point?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Advice for Visitors
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: If you plan to visit the Dunhuang caves, here is some useful advice.
Book your ticket early, because only a few people may enter each cave every day.
Bring a hat and water, since the desert sun is very strong.
Inside the caves, please speak quietly and never touch the walls.
In this way, the wonderful paintings can be kept safe for everyone who comes after us.
exercises.translation_cn: 如果你打算参观敦煌的洞窟,这里有些实用建议:早点订票,因为每天每个洞窟只允许少数人进入;带上帽子和水,因为沙漠的阳光很强;在洞内请轻声说话,切勿触摸墙壁;这样,精美的壁画才能为后来的每个人妥善保存。
